policy_title: Invest in local arts, sport, and culture
stated: Invest an extra £5bn over 5 years for local government spending on arts and culture, including museums, theatres, libraries, and galleries. Protect the night-time economy, permit local authorities to invest in professional sports clubs, and allow access to school sports facilities outside teaching hours.

source.quote: To support local culture and sport, elected Greens will campaign to: • Invest an extra £5bn over 5 years for local government spending on arts and culture to fund keeping local museums, theatres, libraries and art galleries open and thriving. • Protect the night-time economy through a review of planning regulations and giving local authorities the powers to ensure there is space for cultural life. • Permit local authorities to invest in shares in professional sports clubs which operate in their area as a means of maintaining a connection between the club and its community. • Allow access to school sports facilities by local clubs and teams outside teaching hours to ensure maximum use of a valuable resource.

bearing_set.reason: £5bn cultural sector investment and explicit protection of the night-time economy directly affect employment volume, job security, and pay conditions for arts, hospitality, and entertainment workers.

Library investment supports lifelong learning and skills access; opening school sports facilities outside teaching hours extends community (including children's) use of educational infrastructure, touching the 'skills to get on' and educational-access indicators.
£5bn over five years is a material new spending commitment; if unfunded or borrowing-financed, it moves the debt-path and funded-vs-borrowed indicators directly.

Cultural infrastructure investment and night-time economy protection are established drivers of local economic activity, creative-sector productivity, and tourism — moving real living standards and business-dynamism indicators at sub-national level.

Arts, culture, libraries, sports facilities, and night-time venues are primary empirical drivers of social trust, civic participation, and community belonging — the core indicators of this fundamental — making this the policy's most direct outcome bearing.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn real verdicts: the educational-access mechanism (O7), the fiscal cost of a sizeable new spending pledge (O12), local economic multiplier effects (O13), and the direct community-belonging mechanism (O15). Effects on O4 (labour quality) and O14 (inequality) are plausible but too dependent on unspecified implementation details to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage.
